mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 5.5% signals weakening labor market strength, leading to reduced corporate investment and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when UNRATE crosses 5.5% (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in both demand (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) indicates economic expansion, boosting market confidence and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 and INDPRO correlation doesn't predict positive returns (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS >4.5%) raises borrowing costs, dampening equity valuations and generating negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS >4.5% doesn't lead to negative returns in tightening periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Payroll employment (PAYEMS) dropping below 130,000 suggests labor market weakness, reducing consumer spending and causing negative returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS below 130k doesn't consistently cause negative returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising labor demand (PAYEMS) alongside increasing unemployment (UNRATE) indicates labor market contradictions, leading to market uncertainty and negative returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS and UNRATE interaction doesn't predict negative returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising CPIAUCSL indexes signal inflationary pressures, eroding equity value and producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL rising doesn't consistently lead to negative returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Peak quarterly GDP demand (GDPC1) in a late-cycle expansion signals overvaluation, triggering negative returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Late-cycle peaks in GDPC1 don't consistently result in negative returns (p > 0.05).
